evals.prompt: we're thinking about turning on isolatedDeclarations across every package, not just the build projects. what does the TypeScript team actually say about it -- the constraints it imposes, what it buys, and how it interacts with declaration emit? research this before we plan it
evals.expected_output: The response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines covering separate facets (declaration-emit semantics, annotation constraints on authors, packaging/attw interaction), states it will read references/typescript-sources.md before composing briefs, restricts every brief to T1/T2 sources with a TIER field in the findings format, and outlines a synthesis plan naming both Consensus and Contradictions/drift sections.
expectations: Response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines, each scoped to a different facet -- declaration-emit semantics, the annotation constraints isolatedDeclarations imposes on authors, and its packaging/attw interaction must each appear as a separate dispatch with a distinct brief, not merged into one.
The response states it will read references/typescript-sources.md before composing agent briefs to obtain the source allowlist -- it does not inline a self-derived source list.

Every brief names only sources from the T1/T2 allowlist (typescriptlang.org, devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript, github.com/microsoft/TypeScript, nodejs.org, typescript-eslint.io, arethetypeswrong, publint); no brief names Matt Pocock, Total TypeScript, TypeScript Deep Dive, tsconfig/bases, DefinitelyTyped, Stack Overflow, Medium, or any other non-allowlisted source.
The findings format the briefs specify includes a TIER field per source (T1 or T2), and the response states T1 outranks T2 when sources disagree.

The response references the seeded tsconfig.base.json's existing comment (isolatedDeclarations deliberately excluded from base because the tooling project includes tests) to anchor what the research is meant to resolve -- it does not plan the research in a vacuum.
All WOULD-DISPATCH lines appear in the response before any synthesis plan; the planned briefing names both a Consensus and a Contradictions/drift section as distinct headings.

evals.prompt: did TypeScript 7 break anything we'd care about? we're on 6.0.3. give me the actual list of breaking changes, and tell me where you got it from
evals.expected_output: The response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines across different facets of the 6-to-7 delta (compiler defaults, removed options/targets, module-resolution changes), at least one brief names devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript or github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/releases as a first-class source to fetch directly, and the response explicitly states the Breaking-Changes wiki is stale at TS 4.9 and must not be used as the source for current breaking changes.
expectations: Response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines, each scoped to a different facet of the 6-to-7 delta -- compiler defaults, removed options/targets, and module-resolution changes are the minimum expected facets.

At least one WOULD-DISPATCH brief explicitly names devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript or github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/releases as a first-class source to fetch directly, not relying on generic search ranking alone.

The response states that github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/Breaking-Changes is stale at TS 4.9 and must not be used as the source for current (TS 5+) breaking changes -- a response that cites that wiki page as the authoritative current list fails this criterion.

Every GitHub-scoped brief restricts to github.com/microsoft/* or raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/*; no brief targets bare github.com, a different org, or microsoft/typescript-go as a live, separate repository.
WOULD-DISPATCH lines appear in the response before the synthesis plan is described; no repo file is written without explicit user confirmation.

evals.prompt: can we drop the .js extensions from our relative imports now that node strips types natively? and do we need erasableSyntaxOnly? I want to know who actually decides this before we touch tsconfig
evals.expected_output: The response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines across Node's type-stripping semantics, TypeScript's erasableSyntaxOnly/rewriteRelativeImportExtensions flags, and NodeNext resolution's extension requirement, with at least one brief targeting nodejs.org/api/typescript.html and the response stating Node is co-normative T1 on the runtime boundary rather than subordinate to Microsoft.
expectations: Response emits at least 3 distinct WOULD-DISPATCH: Explore lines, each scoped to a different facet -- Node's type-stripping semantics, TypeScript's erasableSyntaxOnly/rewriteRelativeImportExtensions flags, and NodeNext resolution's extension requirement must each appear as a separate dispatch.

At least one WOULD-DISPATCH brief explicitly targets nodejs.org/api/typescript.html, and the response states Node is co-normative T1 on the runtime boundary -- a response treating nodejs.org as a lower tier than typescriptlang.org fails this criterion.
The response states that a Microsoft-vs-Node disagreement on the runtime boundary would be a genuine two-owner conflict to surface, not one to silently resolve in favor of one side.

The response distinguishes this question from typescript-configuration's scope -- it does not answer 'how this repo's tsconfig is wired' in place of researching upstream, and does not promise to edit tsconfig.base.json itself.
Every brief restricts to the T1/T2 allowlist; no brief names a third-party tutorial, blog, or individual author's material.
